steps.notes: Gold passes; signature matches; tests are self-contained asserts (h5 entries are placeholder bool True). BUT the step background derives a DIFFERENT ODE (beta/(mL), A/(mL^2)) than the one the gold/tests/targets encode (beta, A) - undetectable here because all three tests use L=1.0 (and m is not a parameter); see D10 finding.

Gold passes. Signature matches; spec complete (RK4 formulas given, trajectory shape (n+1,2) documented). Tests are weak sanity checks only: a forward-Euler integrator passes all three (see D8 finding).

GOLD FAILS ITS OWN TARGET on this machine (verified twice, deterministic failure): gold selects optimal_dt=min_dt=0.001 -> trajectory shape (10001,2)/(20001,2)/(15001,2), but the frozen h5 targets are the dt=max_dt=10 trajectories, shapes (2,2)/(3,2)/(2,2) -> np.allclose broadcast ValueError. Targets are bit-identical to the dt=10 gold trajectory in all 3 tests.

findings.evidence: KNOWN defect (time.time()-dependent output shape) - VERIFIED and SHARPENED to blocker. Gold's combined metric is gte_norm * sqrt(elapsed) where elapsed = time.time() wall-clock of the dt-run. The frozen h5 targets are BIT-IDENTICAL (np.array_equal True for all 3 tests) to the trajectory computed with optimal_dt = max_dt = 10 (shapes (2,2),(3,2),(2,2); values up to |7.8e3|). But on this machine the measured metrics are: test1 dt=0.001 -> gte=5.42e-10, elapsed=0.114s, metric=1.83e-10 vs dt=10 -> gte=4.69e+01, elapsed=2.9e-05s, metric=2.52e-01 (dt=0.001 wins by 9 orders of magnitude; tests 2 and 3 similar, up to 12 orders). The ONLY way dt=10 can win is if time.time() measured elapsed == 0.0 for the 1-2-step dt=10 run (then metric = gte*sqrt(0) = 0 < anything), which happens on coarse-resolution wall clocks (e.g. Windows time.time() ~15.6 ms ticks) but essentially never on Linux (microsecond resolution). So the frozen target encodes a timer-resolution artifact of the authoring machine. CONSEQUENCE: 'python3 review/tools/steptest.py --problem 78 --step 78.3 --use-gold' FAILS (run twice, deterministic): gold picks dt=0.001, returns shape (10001,2), and np.allclose raises 'operands could not be broadcast together with shapes (10001,2) (2,2)'. No competent solver implementation (nor the official gold itself) can pass this step on the evaluation platform; the failure is a property of the frozen target, not of solver code.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove wall-clock timing from the scored output path entirely: either (a) redefine the metric on a deterministic cost proxy (e.g. number of derivative evaluations or n steps) and regenerate targets, or (b) score only the trajectory at a SPECIFIED dt and drop the timing-based selection. At minimum, regenerate the h5 targets on the actual evaluation platform and loosen the comparison; but any target that depends on time.time() remains machine-dependent and should not be frozen.

findings.evidence: The step background explicitly derives the final ODE as: 'd omega/dt = -(g/L) sin(theta) - beta/(mL) omega + A/(mL^2) cos(alpha t)' (after the torque equation 'tau = -mgL sin(theta) - beta L d theta/dt + A cos(alpha t)' and dividing by mL^2). The gold/tests/targets instead encode domega_dt = -(g/L)*sin(theta) - beta*omega + A*cos(alpha*t) (beta and A used DIRECTLY, i.e. the m and L factors silently absorbed). m is not a function parameter, so a solver following the provided derivation must set m=1 and write beta/L and A/L**2. This background-faithful implementation PASSES all three 78.1 tests (verified via steptest: review/work/78/bg_faithful.py -> PASS) because every 78.1 test uses L=1.0, where the two forms coincide. But all three 78.3 tests use L=0.1/0.5/0.3, where the forms diverge wildly (at 78.3-test-1 params, gold domega=-8.97 vs background domega=+77.46, ~10x and sign-flipped). So the step-1 contract as written silently corrupts step 3 scoring: a solver who trusts the supplied background fails 78.3 with no detectable error at 78.1. (78.3 is currently a blocker anyway, but this defect independently survives any target regeneration.)
findings.suggested_fix: Make the background derivation consistent with the intended equation: state the simplified form d omega/dt = -(g/L) sin(theta) - beta*omega + A*cos(alpha*t) explicitly (i.e. define beta as the angular damping RATE and A as the angular driving acceleration amplitude, absorbing m and L), and fix the intermediate torque/division steps accordingly. Alternatively add a 78.1 test with L != 1 so the two readings are distinguished at the step where the formula is written.

findings.evidence: The prompt's core requirement is 'a fourth-order fixed-time-step Runge-Kutta (RK4) integrator ... Do not use any canned numerical integration routines', but the tests cannot detect a wrong integrator. Test 1 checks final theta against the SHM solution with atol=0.1 while the whole motion has amplitude 0.1 (theta_0=0.1) - the tolerance equals the full signal amplitude; test 2 only checks final_state[0] < 0.1; test 3 only checks not-NaN. A deliberately wrong FORWARD EULER integrator (first-order) passes all three tests under official joint scoring (verified: review/work/78/euler_probe.py -> 'RESULT step 78.2: PASS'). There is no h5 numeric target for this step (placeholder bool True), so nothing pins 4th-order accuracy or even the documented trajectory shape (n+1,2) beyond what test 1's single indexed element exercises.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a test that actually constrains RK4-order accuracy, e.g. compare trajectory[-1] against a tight reference (atol ~1e-8 for dt=0.01, n=1000 undamped pendulum, where RK4 error ~1e-10 but Euler error ~1e-2), or assert the empirical convergence order between dt and dt/2 runs is ~4. Also assert trajectory.shape == (n+1, 2).

findings.evidence: Latent secondary ambiguity (currently masked by the D5 blocker, but it will bite any target regeneration): neither the prompt nor the docstring specifies how the number of RK4 steps is derived from (t0, tf, dt), nor whether the trajectory must actually reach tf. The frozen target requires gold's floor convention n = int((tf-t0)/dt): target test 3 has tf=15, dt=10 -> n=1, shape (2,2), i.e. the 'trajectory of the pendulum system' STOPS AT t=10, never reaching tf=15. A solver using round() or ceil() (to actually cover [t0, tf]) gets n=2 -> shape (3,2) -> shape-mismatch failure. The docstring gives no output shape ('optimized_trajectory: numpy array of floats') so the solver cannot infer the convention. Similarly unstated: that the dt sweep is np.linspace(min_dt, max_dt, num_timesteps) (harmless for the given tests since num_timesteps=2 makes linspace == logspace == endpoints).
findings.suggested_fix: When regenerating this step, specify in the docstring: n = int((tf - t0) / dt) (floor; trajectory may end before tf) and that timesteps are np.linspace(min_dt, max_dt, num_timesteps); or better, choose test parameters where (tf-t0)/dt is an exact integer for every candidate dt.

overall_assessment: Problem 78 is NOT fair to score as-is. Step 78.3 is a hard blocker: the frozen target is bit-identical to the dt=max_dt=10 trajectory, which the gold's own metric only selects when time.time() measures 0.0 elapsed for the fast run (a coarse-timer artifact of the authoring machine) - on the Linux eval platform the gold itself deterministically fails its own target with a shape-mismatch ValueError, so 78.3 scores 0 for every solver including a perfect one. Independently, step 78.1's background derives an ODE (beta/(mL), A/(mL^2)) that contradicts the equation the targets encode (beta, A), undetectable at 78.1 (all tests L=1) but fatal at 78.3 (L=0.1/0.5/0.3); and step 78.2's tests are so weak that a forward-Euler integrator passes a step whose entire point is RK4. Steps 78.1 and 78.2 score correct solutions correctly, but 78.2 also passes wrong ones.
